blocks.content: Jharkhand's demography chapter centres on its rich diversity of Scheduled Tribe communities — the state officially recognises 32 distinct tribal groups, several of which are classified as Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), making this one of the most name-dense tribal-classification chapters in Indian state GS syllabi.

cells: approx 26% — one of the higher ST population shares of any major Indian state

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Jharkhand officially recognises 32 Scheduled Tribes — one of the largest numbers of distinct, individually-recognised tribal communities of any Indian state, a frequently tested headline statistic.

cells: The largest tribal community of Jharkhand (and one of India's largest tribal groups overall); concentrated in the Santhal Pargana region; associated with the 1855-56 Santhal Hul (Chapter 3)

A major tribal community, historically centred around Ranchi district; associated with Birsa Munda and the Ulgulan (Chapter 3); traditionally organised under the 'Munda-Manki' village-and-cluster self-governance system

A major Dravidian-language-speaking tribal community (linguistically distinct from most other Jharkhand tribes, which are predominantly Austroasiatic/Munda-language speakers), concentrated in the Chota Nagpur plateau area
Concentrated in the Kolhan area (Singhbhum region); traditionally governed under their own 'Munda-Manki' system, similar in structure to the Munda tribe's governance tradition
Numerous smaller tribal communities across the state, each with distinct traditional occupations, languages/dialects and cultural practices

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: The Oraon tribe is linguistically distinct from most of Jharkhand's other major tribes — Oraon speak a Dravidian language (Kurukh), whereas the Santhal, Munda and Ho speak Austroasiatic (Munda-family) languages — a frequently tested linguistic-classification fact that cuts across the state's tribal demography.

items: Jharkhand has 8 officially designated Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) — communities characterised by pre-agricultural technology, extremely low or stagnant population growth, and very low literacy, warranting special central and state protective/developmental attention.

These include the Asur, Birhor, Birajia, Korwa, Mal Paharia, Parhaiya, Sauria Paharia, and Savar communities — each numerically small and, in several cases, historically forest-dwelling or semi-nomadic in traditional lifestyle.

The Birhor community, traditionally forest-dwelling hunter-gatherers known for rope-making from forest fibres, and the Sauria/Mal Paharia communities of the Rajmahal Hills area, are among the most frequently cited examples in PVTG-focused exam questions for this state.
Hindi is the official language of Jharkhand and the most widely understood language across the state.

Santhali (an Austroasiatic language, written in the distinctive Ol Chiki script devised by Pandit Raghunath Murmu in the 20th century) holds official 'second language' status in the state and is included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution — a significant linguistic-recognition milestone for a tribal language.

Other tribal languages/dialects — Mundari, Kurukh (Oraon), Ho, Kharia, among others — remain in active local use, alongside regional Indo-Aryan languages such as Nagpuri, Khortha, Kurmali and Panchpargania spoken by various non-tribal and mixed communities of the state.

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Santhali is written in the Ol Chiki script (devised by Pandit Raghunath Murmu) and is included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution — a distinctive script-and-constitutional-recognition fact frequently tested for this specific tribal language.

items: Population (2011): approx 3.30 crore; ST share approx 26%; SC share approx 12%; 32 officially recognised Scheduled Tribes.
Major tribes: Santhal (largest, Santhal Pargana), Munda (Ranchi area, Birsa Munda's community), Oraon (Dravidian-language-speaking), Ho (Kolhan/Singhbhum area).
8 PVTGs in Jharkhand: Asur, Birhor, Birajia, Korwa, Mal Paharia, Parhaiya, Sauria Paharia, Savar.
Santhali language: written in the Ol Chiki script (devised by Pandit Raghunath Murmu); included in the Constitution's Eighth Schedule.
